Citation_Information.author_list: Barnouin, O.; Daly, M.; Espiritu, R.; OSIRIS-REx Altimetry Working Group
Citation_Information.description:
The shape of (101955) Bennu is obtained using stereophotoclinometry and/or lidar techniques.
The model has the format
v x1 y1 z1 v x2 y2 z2 v x3 y3 z3 (etc.)
f i1 j1 k1 f i2 j2 k2 (etc.)
where the letter 'v' denotes a vertex and the letter 'f' denotes a triangular facet. A comment with # is provided at the beginning of the file providing More details about the shape. See OSIRIS-REx Altimetry SIS for more details.

Investigation_Area.name: Origins, Spectral Interpretation, Resource Identification, Security, Regolith Explorer (OSIRIS-REx)

Observing_System_Component.name: OSIRIS-REx Spacecraft
Observing_System_Component.description: The sub-systems that comprise the OSIRIS-REx spacecraft are the telecommunications subsystem; the power sub-system; the propulsion sub-system; and the guidance, navigation, control (GNC) sub-system. These sub-systems work together to communicate with the Earth, deliver the spacecraft to the target asteroid, and navigate around the asteroid. The spacecraft hosts a navigation camera system (TAGCAMS), a science camera system (OCAMS), a visible and infrared spectrometer (OVIRS), a thermal emission spectrometer (OTES), and a laser altimeter (OLA). The collection, retrieval, storage and return of the asteroid sample is conducted using the Touch-And-Go Sample Acquisition System (TAGSAM), and the Sample Return Capsule (SRC). The combined spacecraft sub-systems and the hosted complement of instrumentation allows the OSIRIS-REx mission to gather data, collect a sample, and safely return the sample to Earth.

Table_Character.description: The VERTEX_TABLE is the first part, describing the positions of the vertices of the shape model. The floating point numbers x1 y1 z1 are the coordinates of vertex 1, and so on (vertices are implicitly numbered beginning with 1). The origin is the center of mass, and the axes are the principal axes of the shape model. This coordinate system should not be used to define a cartographic system, as the principal axes are not uniquely determined due to the symmetry of the shape. The z-axis is the spin axis or positive pole. The units are kilometers. The linking of vertices into facets is provided in the FACET_TABLE.

Field_Character.name: Vertex Flag
Field_Character.description: A 'v', indicating this record contains the coordinates of a vertex

Field_Character.name: X Vertex Coordinate
Field_Character.description: The x coordinate of the vertex

Field_Character.name: Y Vertex Coordinate
Field_Character.description: The y coordinate of the vertex

Field_Character.name: Z Vertex Coordinate
Field_Character.description: The z coordinate of the vertex

Table_Character.description: The FACET_TABLE is the second part of the shape model file providing the linking of vertices into facets. The integers i1 j1 k1 are the indices of the 3 vertices that form triangular facet 1, and so on.

Field_Character.name: Facet Flag
Field_Character.description: An 'f', indicating this record contain the indices of three vertices defining a single, triangular facet

Field_Character.name: Vertex 1
Field_Character.description: Index of the first vertex (record number in the preceding table)
